question: Which of the following antitussive can lead to hallucinations
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Dextromethorphan" -> "NMDA receptor antagonist" -> "increased risk of dissociative effects" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Diphenhydramine" -> "anticholinergic properties" -> "CNS effects including confusion" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Morphine" -> "opioid receptor agonist" -> "CNS depression" -> "possible altered mental status" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Aprepitant" -> "substance P/neurokinin 1 receptor antagonist" -> "not commonly associated with hallucinations" -> "unlikely to cause hallucinations" -> 20%
analysis: Dextromethorphan is known to cause hallucinations, especially at high doses, due to its action as an NMDA receptor antagonist. While morphine can also cause hallucinations, it is primarily an opioid used for pain relief and not typically classified as an antitussive in standard practice. Diphenhydramine, an antihistamine, can cause sedation and anticholinergic effects but is less commonly associated with hallucinations. Aprepitant is primarily used as an antiemetic and does not have a significant association with hallucinations. Therefore, the best-supported option is dextromethorphan.
